In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
RFs and especially CNNs are very competitive methods for Persian handwritten digit classification, and they can outperform other methods in terms of recognition rate and speed.
RFs are a good choice for small datasets and when the computational resources are limited, and CNNs are a good option if the computational resources are abundant.
CNNs and RFs are competitive with each other and both outperform the state of the art on the Hoda database, while CNNs are the fastest and RFs are the most accurate.
